51600687.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to PKM2 (unknown origin) assessed as dissociation constant by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - SPR assay: 4.2.1.4. SPR assay. The SPR assay was performed on a Biacore T200 instrument (GE Healthcare, Chicago, IL, USA) to test whether B4 binds to PKM2. First, the two flow cells of the CM5 sensor chip (GE Healthcare, Chicago, IL, USA) were activated for 420 s with freshly prepared 50 mM NHS and 200 mM carbodiimide hydrochloride (EDC, Sigma-Aldrich, St. Louis, MO, USA). Afterwards, the PKM2 protein was diluted in 10 mM NaAC (pH = 5.0) and immobilized on CM5 sensor chips for 10 min. After completion of the amine-coupling reaction, the remaining sites were blocked by 1 M ethanolamine hydrochloride (pH = 8.5). The B4 was used at concentrations ranging from 3.125 to 50 μM (3.125, 6.25, 12.5, 25, 50 μM). The assay was then performed according to the instructions provided by GE Healthcare. The parameters of SPR were set as follows: temperature, 25 °C; flow rate, 20 μL/min; contact time, 300 s; dissociation time, 600 s. The equilibrium dissociation constant (Kd) for B4 was obtained to evaluate the binding affinity by using the BIA evaluation 2.0 (GE Healthcare) supposing a 1: 1 binding ratio.
original_paragraph.Figure 3 caption: Fig. 3. B4 covalently interacts with PKM2. (A) The stabilization of PKM2 was detected by cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA). (B) The direct interaction between B4 and PKM2 was detected by surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assay. (C) LC-MS/MS analysis of B4-PKM2 adducted peptide CC(B4)SGAIIVLTK.
original_paragraph.Figure 3B data: The sensorgram in Figure 3B shows the response (RU) over time (s) for B4 at concentrations of 3.125 μM, 6.25 μM, 12.5 μM, 25 μM, and 50 μM. The plot includes calculated values: ka (1/Ms)=1.12E+04, kd(1/s)=0.02773, Kd(M)=2.48E-06, Chi²(RU²)=3.46.
